I saw her very displeased and serious:

I do not want it to be that way.

I could not avoid telling her:

How odd you are!

36 She told me that a certain person would have delivered a child on such a day and after she came to inform me that it was not yet time, that there were still various days and she made me feel || that everything would have gone well.

MS 7 – pp. 1 – 28

Light upon the spirit of a sister

1 January 1885. My sufferings are without compare and the sight of my horrible malice makes me sad till agony. To see whatever is in that depth terrifies me. Oh, if I could be able to see when and how I committed that wickedness!

My God is that abyss for me? Is whatever I see for my greater confusion? What pain is this? How many graces my Good grants me!

To see very clearly those who live deluded to belong to my God…

2 This he made me see in a very clear way. In addition it is for me one of the worst pains || to see these creatures believed holy and me the infamous…

Instead to see the contrary, is not this something additional to my abyss?

One morning I was kneeling in the chapel and I felt pushed to stand up; what did I see? A lay person kneeling and praying. I looked at her and I said:

This is a postulant, who came!

She had an ash coloured dress, a black apron with a blue ribbon, a 3 black with coloured border scarf on her head. || She stood up to go out and since she came nearer to me I was persuaded she was a lay person.

After some minutes she came back.

Who could she be – I said – a sister?

And soon I was informed. But she has not always been a sister. I stayed in prayer.

What do you want to say, my Love?

Away with this one, if not… Her will is such that, she is not a Daughter of St. Anne!

I called the superior and I asked for information and I found out that she was really a bad person. Oh, dear Jesus!

Another morning I was absorbed and I saw a dear beautiful child; it stayed near my face || for quite some time and then it disappeared. 4 There was also a Reformed

Franciscan friar171 in the air with open arms, very big, and tall, still young with a red face.

This remained impressed in me in such a way that it seemed to me I saw him. I heard nothing, but the whole day

I had strong snatches on the side that I had to struggle to repress. My Love!

Passage of beasts and stars at night

I would like to describe well what my Love does in me in my poor ribs but it is useless because I cannot find phrases to describe it. ||

1885. 5 The torment I felt this day is such that it is a torture.

The afflictions were without compare, of every kind.

At night the passage of the beasts has become a terrible torment. There are of every kind: big ones.

What a fright! They scream so loudly and fearfully and they beat themselves. Oh, what pain is for me the night!

6 A star, now small and then a big one; now a cry and when it seems to sleep a loud calling, and finally it would need much if I must describe every thing. ||

While I prayed fervently to the Blessed Virgin to have a grace I desired much, a strong voice said to me: - “You will have it.”

I really see already the effects. How many graces I received from the Blessed Virgin! I see clearly that these torments are allowed by my Good for his Work. Soon the church will be completed and not as many heads work well as the Holy Mother St. Anne would like. To repair this and see that everything goes as well as my Good desires I must suffer. || 7 I see it clearly but this ass is so worn out that it twists in many ways. The enemy even used creatures and for this I felt much pain because it is true that they offend my Good.

“I never did anything in the Work of the Lord: it is only he who works”

Oh, my sweet Love, to see so clearly the falsehood inside the creatures who try to persuade me…

But how can I believe when I see more clearly than the eyes could see what they tell me is false?

8 Oh, what a pain to see || my Good offended!

I suffer so much that the bones of my stomach seem to become like wax; and I am not deceived because unfortunately the truth of what I say is discovered. Moreover while I sustain such truth, some strength and something I do not understand assists me to bear it and gives me courage.

9 Oh, I will always say, until I have the voice, that I never did anything in the Work of the Lord: it is only he who works and does everything and this ass has nothing else but humiliation || seeing always clearly its nothingness and less than nothingness. Poor me, what will I get from such an unhappy ass! My Love, consume me with your love; I want nothing else.

The pure suffering without any comfort

The sufferings in which I find myself keep me so mute and insensible to everything that nothing is helpful to raise me up. I feel a gloomy, deep pain and the nearing of a bigger tempest. I try to understand what I could do to have a bit of relief or at least to understand from where my suffering comes; but not, everything gives me pain. The exhaustion of the whole person does || not allow me to desire anything.

10 But from some time I see a ray of light and in me arises for a while the desire to be able to speak and expose everything to my guide. In that moment I feel some relief only in the desire but soon I fall back and I find myself as if for me there is nothing and that I could desire nothing, that for me everything is finished.

Pure suffering without comfort remains for me.

11 I am unable to desire || the smallest thing; for me everything is emptiness, without understanding and not even having the faculty of desiring anything.

I am boldly thrown in this lethargy where nothing is understood; only pure suffering is felt.

All around is arid and the mind is so still in its position that it could be said there is no remedy. In the unfortunate state in which I am 12 found even the prayer which has always been my comfort is for me a real suffering because I see closely that the Being of my life || has abandoned me and unfortunately I merit it because I serve him very badly . But only he is in me and I live only for him.

Called to Rome for the affair of the Rule (of the Sons of St. Anne?)

Oh, finally today, 15 September I understood the motif of my much suffering. A letter that arrived from Rome from a superior A. informed me that I have been called for the affair of the Rules. What a terrible suffering!

Well, everything that the bad devil, the enemy was making, all the uproar is explained. 13 This evening I am calm;

the diabolic action will be crushed by my Good, and the victory is sure; || the filthy beast will be ashamed.

I fear nothing, only an interior cheerfulness assures me that my Good is nearing and only he is all my immense happiness. I desire nothing else. Yes, yes, I delight because soon I will have the much desired grace.

Therefore, I can say that from such terrible news I have got great good. My anxiety will end at least partially.

How will I come out from such a mess? 14 My Good, || he takes me out from everything and with full victory. I feel strength without compare, without having to battle because that is what my God always does. When this ass must work, he increases the strength; when the work is less, then it has less strength and suffers more because of the sickness and always seems breathing its last even while at work. 15 Perhaps, according to my Good the sufferings do not seem sufficient || to expiate my sins; unfortunately I have them and I always suffer.

My Good, perhaps because of my sins I have merited to be in such a cruel state!

Today, not even the absolution I could receive in union with my Good! Oh, something which I could say, I do not remember had ever happened to me. The priest was giving me the absolution and I wandered with the mind on useless things. In the past I could never dream of such disturbance! 16 And yet, even that sacred moment… || What I suffered after I cannot describe. That ugly monster does all things and tries to be strong; it always torments me and this is why I cannot avoid lamenting. Today it has become clear what the intended lesson was of that beast which carried in its legs some long papers together with the register of documents. The length and the volume were the same…

Here is the explanation: it was our Rule. || 17 The enemy succeeded to make in a way that they put some notes which were not good for the Work of the Lord and it could have lost much. But the filth succeeded. However, whatever it believes to have achieved will be destroyed. They will be unbound and more beautiful and the victory will be sure.

Oh, I remember that it made me laugh when I thought. The sight of that black beast as charcoal with long legs such that to be able to hold || those long papers… 18 It seemed a notary and was completely busy; it passed above the bed and ran on the other side of the room. What an ugly mail-carrier! I laughed much though what it produced in me was terrible.

And all this happened. It has already been announced from yesterday severely that I felt something within me so terrible that I was almost unable to sustain such wound. It is painful to see oneself… Oh, what mortal pains! || 19 Now I wait for another clearing of a beast which I saw one of these evenings.

There were other beasts and one almost in the shape of a man, of a red flesh; two on each side of this beast carried it slowly.

It was a bit more than a meter above the bed in this accompaniment and they stopped because they were labouring much to carry it; they dragged it. Oh, what a fright!

20 A strong || interior trembling took me and it seemed that they shook all my nerves. Who could it be? I do not say all the thoughts that passed in my mind. I formed billions, but I never succeeded to guess one. Enough! This is what my Good allows and I resigned whatever is his will I am fully in accord.

Yes my sweet Love, only for you and nothing more! I want nothing because I am nothing; everything is yours, my Love! || 21 I always feel a strong impulse to work for the sons of St. Anne. My Good what can I do?

I was thinking this way because the outline of the Rule that I had and which was inspired by my Good, I do not find it anymore. I know I gave it to the Father but it cannot be found. Is this loss one of the proofs that the Sons of St. 22 Anne must not be founded? Is what I feel and the new circumstances which are always presented to open the way to this beautiful Congregation all illusions? || Oh, I fear that it is the work of …

Alas, this afflicts me because I would like to be calm in these days of much work. No, I always feel some interior happiness and with a strong impulse to do it. But how my Good?

Well, as I said above, I complained with my Good and now the loss…

An interior voice said to me:

Write, because you will have as those which cannot be found, write!

23 Well, I promised that || this night I will do everything to find a moment to write them.

Yes, I will do it, and you, my Good, guide the pen, make suggestions to me and they will be written soon and with your powerful help they will be observed. Even these will be sons of the heart of the Holy Mother St. Anne and faithful cooperators in your vineyard which is in great need. 24 Oh, my Love, when that thought controls me it is a true joy that my poor spirit delights and all in beautiful and holy thoughts runs || to see the finished work!

Everything is established by my Good and I already see the Sons of the heart of the saint all concentrated and full of the love of God; working for the glory of God, converting sinners, evangelising the whole world and giving to the work of the Daughters the most beautiful distinction. 25 Oh, blessed dream! Moment of paradise that makes me forget everything and only the desire that everything may be carried out dominates and occupies the whole mind and it does not allow obstacles to block its way.172 ||

Advantage of the arid obedience to the director

Evening of 13 September 1885. I received many things in these days. How my Good showed me clearly the preciousness of patience and resignation to his will in everything!

I clearly saw that who directed my soul was pleasing to my God and Jesus was very pleased that I stayed under such arid obedience. I follow it scrupulously and I see clearly its effects.

I wanted to ask for a grace to the Lord in my own way but I was prohibited by my guide. I would have liked to ignore such obedience and make the prayer. Oh, an invincible force kept me and I had to stop. ||

26 In the same way when I go to confess regularly to the confessor of the community his words and his absolution bring me different effect. But when I go to confession to the one who guides me, arid and hasty as it is, I find no comfort.

Nevertheless in my soul I feel some kind of progress. I see clearly the smallest imperfections, and the faults that I could have not known unless my Good had made me known. 27 I feel peace and resignation in all the adversities and a strong desire || to be forgotten by all. I feel pleasure thinking that I will be despised by the whole world. ||

notes.memorie-en-fn122: Caterina Fieschi from Genoa (1447 – 1510), Franciscan Tertiary, a great mystic, is very much venerated by the people of Genoa. She was canonised by Clement XII in 1737.

notes.memorie-en-fn126: This is an evident mistake as happens many times to Mother Rosa at the beginning of the subsequent month. The date is 3 August; in fact the feast of Mother St. Anne was recent, 26 July.
notes.memorie-en-fn127: The feast of the Stigmata of St. Francis of Assisi was celebrated on 17 December. It is a point of reference to situate chronologically the experiences she had.
notes.memorie-en-fn128: It is not precisely known who this Friar Pacifico is.
notes.memorie-en-fn129: This small niece, daughter of Carlotta, called by a pet name “Rosetto” died following the epidemic of canina cough and diphtheria.
notes.memorie-en-fn130: Father Angelo Ricchini is the priest of Sampierdarena with whom the Foundress had a long judiciary quarrel. In reality he died in September 1878.
notes.memorie-en-fn131: The Servant of God professed special devotion to the first Person of the Holy Trinity. In the Institute the month of January was dedicated to the Eternal Father (cf. Spiritual Portrait, p. 177).
notes.memorie-en-fn132: We do not know who this “wise and holy Franciscan” could be. It seems that during the visit to the houses of Sicily he encouraged her to carry on the plan of the foundation of the Sons of St. Anne: an Institute of priests destined to work in the Church for the glory of God, the conversion of sinners, for the evangelisation and the formation of the Daughters of St. Anne.
notes.memorie-en-fn133: The real content of the symbol of the three drops of blood revealed to her in a vision in the past, which was unclear at the beginning, became clearer as the Foundress received more enlightenment on the “three Orders” God wanted her to found.
notes.memorie-en-fn134: The manuscript says: “1882” but it is a mistake because the journey of the Servant of God to Sicily took place during the first months of 1883.
notes.memorie-en-fn135: The transfer of the General House from Piacenza to Rome was advised to the Foundress by the same Holy See. That was convenient for an Institute of pontifical right with a growing universal zeal. Two years earlier, following the bitterness she felt for the suspicions on her way of managing the goods of the Institute, she was tempted to ask for substitution in the government. Instead now she finds herself to be necessary; she wants to live to be useful to the Work of God holding the reins in her hand.
notes.memorie-en-fn136: The fact of the grave sickness and of the miraculous healing is widely documented. She was diagnosed with peritonitis on 29 April; telegrams were sent to the main houses. The same was done on the occasion of her healing that took place after two days. In this “sacrifice” Mother Rosa saw the price requested by God for the work of the General House as it was announced to her the year before in the vision of 4 September in which an angel with a chalice in his hand, that reevoked the prayer of Jesus in the garden, appeared to her. A voice announced that she should be prepared to drink it until the last drop. She attributed the healing to the intercession of the Virgin Mater gratiae et misericordiae, the title of the Madonnina of the venerable Father Bernardo M.Clausi from whom it passed to the hands of Father Tornatore. She was venerated in Piacenza in the chapel of the Mother House. The church of the General House in Rome will be dedicated to her.
notes.memorie-en-fn137: The Servant of God liked to see the Institute as a ship that ploughed the sea of the world in waves as she held the reins. In the book Travagli e conforti (pp.73-78, 317-347) she will describe amply the events of the ship of the Saviour on which waves the flag “Suffering-Love”. The enthusiastic collaborator of the work in Rome for whose conversion she prayed was no other than her brother Federico Gattorno who from his youth has been far from faith. The Servant of God offered prayers and penances for him and at the same time she was very understanding with him.
notes.memorie-en-fn138: The sanctuary of Our Lady of Oropa is the most popular in the Piedmont. Mother Rosa went there in pilgrimage at the beginning of September 1885 accompanied by her two secretaries and by her brother Federico whose conversion she entrusted to the Virgin. This was not in vain, because after some time Federico was seriously sick; when he became well again, he decided to settle his state having a canonical marriage with his partner on 21 November 1885, in the chapel of the Daughters of St. Anne, with much consolation of his sister.
notes.memorie-en-fn139: Who was this P. le (provincial?) whose death was announced by the Foundress with the sign of a “big globe of fire”? It cannot be a provincial because at that time there were only two and they were both alive; Sister Anne del Salvatore will die on 7 June of the following year.
notes.memorie-en-fn140: After many years without a spiritual director, but always convinced of being in need of one, finally she decided to consult a “holy and wise religious”. The reply of the father left her uncertain as to the will of God. Should she place herself under the direction of the father or should she continue to be guided by her Good? The fact is that in the month of March 1884 she placed herself under the direction of the General Minister of the Franciscan Minors; Father Bernardino da Portogruaro, well known in the history of his Order for having oriented it wisely towards the restoration after the long trial of the suppressions. The cause of his canonisation has been introduced.
notes.memorie-en-fn141: She is Sister Anne Francesca Savignone, niece of Mother Rosa, daughter of her sister Elisa, who died in Piacenza on 25 June 1884, considered a woman of much virtue.
notes.memorie-en-fn142: The direction of Father Bernardino da Portogruaro did not fill the emptiness as the Servant of God expected but it became the cause of greater anxiety. On one side she was limited from bodily penances and the night watches and on the other side she missed the enlightening communication she hoped to find in him. What displeased her most was the awareness that now Jesus has interrupted his divine direction.
notes.memorie-en-fn143: In fact a wide range epidemic of cholera had broken out which brought desolation in all of Southern Europe for more than two years.
notes.memorie-en-fn144: Monsignor Scalabrini, Bishop of Piacenza, welcomed favourably the availability of Mother Rosa regarding the direction of an Institute of Dumbdeaf who were also oriented to religious life and opened in 1880. The community of the Tertiary of St. Anne perpetual Adorers of the Blessed Sacrament, started on 8 December 1884. However, the orientation given by the Bishop did not seem to agree with the project of Mother Rosa (cf. above, year 1882, note 3).
notes.memorie-en-fn145: On the project of the foundation of the Sons of St. Anne (cf. above, Year 1882, note 2).
notes.memorie-en-fn146: G.F. stands for the “General of the Franciscans”. The Servant of God is always more convinced of the will of God regarding the direction of Father Bernardino da Portogruaro; however, she is to master the interior reaction at the thought that she must renounce the guidance and teaching of her Love as she is used to experience it. She foresaw an invincible repugnance to open herself fully to the above mentioned father.
notes.memorie-en-fn147: The torment derived from the submission to the spiritual director returned in an obsessive way. “I must wait for months to have a word and then…” Father Bernardino was frequently away from Rome to mind his office of minister general. It seems that in addition to telling him verbally about her intimate life she also gave him some parts of her Memoirs to read; this fact increased her tension more.
notes.memorie-en-fn148: The initials P.G. may indicate the “Father General” of the Friars Minor, her spiritual father; but also the priest Don Gennaro Granito Pignatelli di Belmonte, with whom, on the occasion of the journey to Sicily, she began a very close spiritual relationship. notes.memorie-en-fn149: “A religious G.” is perhaps a Jesuit.
notes.memorie-en-fn150: Mother Rosa had difficulty to reveal to Father Bernardino da Potogruaro her intimate experiences, the extraordinary graces and her penances.
notes.memorie-en-fn151: The “big house” without doubt is the General House which was being completed.
notes.memorie-en-fn152: Here she found a solution to the long tension regarding the spiritual direction: “subjected but not bound or tied”. The supreme Good returns to be her true guide. It does not mean a real alternative option between the obedience to the director and the freedom of spirit but a harmonious joining of the two.
notes.memorie-en-fn153: Regarding the “oil of the Eternal Father,” look above Section I, First report, note 9.
notes.memorie-en-fn154: “A hard, severe and arid obedience”, the direction of Father Bernardino da Potogruaro is quite different from being a refugee in difficulties. The Servant of God kept it only because the one who guided her wanted it.
notes.memorie-en-fn155: The sense of Church was very strong in Rosa Gattorno. It is to be noted how she spent Good Friday. The mystical participation to the passion of Christ made her experience what the Head of the church suffers in his members.
notes.memorie-en-fn156: The Servant of God without saying compares the style of Pius IX with whom she found it easy to have private audiences and the pontificate of Leo XIII when the Roman curia acquired an organic aspect; every department carried on its function in the respective sector, with delegated authority. The Pope was always busier with issues having universal character. On the other hand in those decades the religious Institutes multiplied with such abundance in all the nations that it was not possible to follow every one individually. On 5 April, Sunday of Easter, she had the consolation of receiving the Communion from the hands of the Pope in the Sistine Chapel. A Few days later she was received in audience and she presented to the Holy Father the book, The Daughters of St. Anne during the cholera of 1884, printed by Cardinal Sanfelice, Archbishop of Naples. The heroism with which the Daughters of St. Anne gave their best in the wide epidemic contributed very much to the good of the Institute.
notes.memorie-en-fn157: He is the Blessed Ludovico da Casoria, Reformed Franciscan, a great social apostle, founder of two religious congregations. He died in Naples on 30 March 1885. He was canonised by Jon Paul II in 1992.
notes.memorie-en-fn158: The foresight of the Servant of God will become partially true. Leo XIII will live until 20 July 1903. He will be succeeded by Pius X (1903 – 1914).
notes.memorie-en-fn159: It is a correct observation, fruit of a long experience. There are still religious who close themselves to their superiors, responsible for the good of all their subjects; while they try to make good impression to their confessor who does not know them in real life.
notes.memorie-en-fn160: By now the problem of the direction of Father Bernardino da Portogruaro seems solved. The Servant of God feels dependent on him through an obedience of faith, lived even from a distance, in his long absences. However, the true guide is the supreme Good (look above note 3, 5 and 7).
notes.memorie-en-fn161: The sister to whom Mother Rosa wrote on 1st May 1885 is Sister Anne Giuseppa Troni, superior of the Mother House in Piacenza, very esteemed by the Servant of God.
notes.memorie-en-fn162: About the foundation of the Sons of St. Anne look above, Year 1882, note 2; Year 1884, note 8.
notes.memorie-en-fn163: Sister Anne del Salvatore Orsi, superior of the house of Palermo, died on 7 June 1885. The spiritual tuning that united Mother Rosa with Sister Anne del Salvatore became tighter after her death.
notes.memorie-en-fn164: The Foundress attributed to the effective help of Sister Anne del Salvatore the successful conclusion of the long process of the Constitutions. In fact on 26 July, the feast of St. Anne of 1885, they were approved for ten years.

notes.memorie-en-fn167: At the beginning of the foundation after six months of novitiate the young were sent into the houses where there was urgent need (Summarium, p. 522); but after as we see here, the Foundress preferred that they start the novitiate after showing sincerity of their vocation in the exercise of charity.
notes.memorie-en-fn168: It is very probable that she had this experience on the feast of St. Francis of Assisi, on 4 October.
notes.memorie-en-fn169: About the miraculous healing, the Servant of God was convinced that they were liberations from diabolic possession; look above, Year 1880, note 2.
notes.memorie-en-fn170: It is not sure who this “prince” for whose soul the Servant of God prays and offers penances was.
notes.memorie-en-fn171: “Reformed Franciscan” that is, belonging to one of the reformed Orders of St. Francis that came up in XVI century from the Observers: the Reformed. To this belonged Father Bernardino da Portogruaro and the Blessed Ludovico da Casoria whom we already know. In 1897 Leo XIII united the reforms of the Alcantarini, Recolletti and the Reformed with the Observant in the same Order of Friar Minors.
notes.memorie-en-fn172: Certainly this time, it is not about the Rule or Constitutions of the Daughters of St. Anne, approved ad decennum on 26 July 1885. 36 From the context it seems to refer to the statutes of the male branch of the Sons of St. Anne, about whose project of foundation the Foundress speaks very frequently throughout 1885. Mother Rosa hints about a “sketch of Rule” which she wrote “inspired” by God. She gave it to Father (Tornatore). On 5 March from Rome she wrote to Sister Anne Giuseppa Troni asking her to send “the manuscript of the Rule” which was on the table of the Father, but the sketch was never found. This mysterious disappearance made her think that perhaps the much caressed project was not according to God’s plan. She fears that someone was opposing it in the Roman curia. From the chronology it appears she made a journey to Rome after having received the communication from the Sacred Congregation but we do not know the outcome. Meanwhile Monsignor Granito Pignatelli di Belmonte on his own took the first steps supporting the project of Mother Rosa. On 6 December in a private audience which he was granted, he asked Pope Leo XIII to institute the Sons of St. Anne. The pope ordered him to present a written request which he did after two days through Monsignor Marzolini. He was advised to start the Work first in Naples so that he may forward the request afterwards with the commendation of the Archbishop.
